title: Register Account
description: Create and verify a personal account by email/code or supported Google entry, complete any account setup and accept required current Terms/Privacy before personalised access.
pre: The patient is not authenticated with a completed account, or is completing a new account's verification/setup.
post: A verified account and required setup/terms acceptance allow Profile or Home routing. Cancelled or failed entry does not grant personalised access; backend retention is a separate configured policy.
flow: Open Register and enter username, email, password and confirmation.
Validate required values and password/confirmation rules; keep invalid fields identifiable and submission protected from repeated taps.
Submit registration.
Request account creation and a six-digit verification email through the authentication repository; show progress or an actionable provider/service error.
Enter the received code, or request resend after the cooldown.
Verify through the authentication service and apply the client attempt policy; an accepted code activates the account.
Complete any required provider-account setup and read the current Terms/Privacy.
Check whether current-version acceptance, health-data consent or an age/guardian declaration is required before the personalisation route.
Accept the required declarations, or decline.
Persist a versioned acceptance when valid. Declining ends the entry without personalised access.
Continue to Profile or Home.
Open mandatory profile setup when incomplete, otherwise Home; restore account reminder scheduling without blocking navigation.
alternatives: A1: Google entry: check provider availability, open the browser flow and complete required username/password setup for a new provider account before the same terms/profile routing.
A2: Invalid/expired code or attempt limit: explain the error; allow the configured resend path instead of treating the account as activated.
A3: Cancel: discard unsaved form state. Cancelling incomplete Google setup invokes its signed-in incomplete-account cleanup; unverified-account retention remains backend-configured.
A4: A required guardian/age or health-data declaration is absent: retain the terms form and block continuation until corrected or declined.
exceptions: E1: Authentication/email service failure or timeout: retain form state and offer retry.
E2: Google/browser cancellation or unavailable provider: return to account entry without a fabricated successful login.
E3: Acceptance persistence failure: keep the consent form and explain retry; do not treat the current version as accepted.
notes: Username/password/code validation follows current AppConstants and authentication repository policies.
Supabase Auth handles password hashing and code verification; the mobile UI does not compare stored password hashes.
Six-digit email verification and provider verification are distinct from current-version terms/health-data consent.
Adult/minor declarations must be consistent with later profile age; the current account flow handles the required guardian form.
Scheduled cleanup jobs are backend deployment configuration, not a guaranteed phone background action.

title: Login Account
description: Authenticate by email/password, restored session or enabled Google entry, then finish required setup/current terms before routing to Profile or Home.
pre: The patient is at account entry or the application is restoring a saved session.
post: A permitted authenticated session reaches Profile/Home after required entry checks; invalid, cancelled or declined entry does not enter personalised workflows.
flow: Open the application or Login and enter valid credentials when requested.
Check a stored session and local inactivity policy, or validate login fields and request authentication.
Submit login or choose an enabled Google entry.
Handle unverified/provider/lockout states through the relevant verification/provider flow rather than assuming every failure is an incorrect password.
Complete any required provider setup or verification.
Resolve the authenticated account and determine whether the current Terms/Privacy version or age/guardian declaration requires review.
Accept required terms and explicit health-data consent, or decline.
Save a valid acceptance before navigation; declining clears account entry and personalised access.
Continue into the application.
Route incomplete profiles to Profile and complete profiles to Home; synchronise reminders for the signed-in account.
alternatives: A1: Valid restored session: skip credential re-entry but still perform required account-setup/current-terms/profile checks.
A2: Forgotten password: request/verify the reset code, set a valid new password and return to Login; use the same account-existence-neutral confirmation.
A3: Unverified email: offer code verification/resend before activated access.
A4: Google unavailable/cancelled: retain a usable email/password entry path.
A5: Current Terms/Privacy or age declaration changed: review it before Profile/Home; declining does not bypass the gate.
exceptions: E1: Invalid credentials/field or temporary lockout: explain the relevant state and retain usable entry values.
E2: Authentication service unavailable or timeout: show retry without creating a session.
E3: Terms acceptance write failure or session change: keep or restart the appropriate entry state; never route another account's delayed result.
notes: The app's local inactivity policy is three days since use/renewal; underlying authentication-token expiry remains provider-managed.
Provider linking/setup follows the authentication backend contract, not an assumption that any typed email proves ownership.
Current-version consent precedes personalisation; saved history is not altered by opening or declining the entry forms.

title: Manage Profile
description: Complete or update body measurements, supported conditions/status, physical limitations and specific foods to avoid; derive risk/safety limits and optionally refresh diet plans.
pre: An authenticated account is available. Terms/age declarations must be consistent with the account workflow.
post: An accepted profile/version and derived limits are stored. Diet plans change only if the patient agrees to refresh and generation succeeds; logged history is retained.
flow: Open Profile and choose a section to edit.
Retrieve the stored profile, lookup lists and current connection state; preserve unsaved section values.
Enter age, gender, weight and height.
Validate configured ranges and combined BMI plausibility; display calculated BMI.
Select supported conditions/status answers, limitations and foods to avoid.
Search/group the choices; hide Other as a new condition and retain legacy saved declarations without silently clearing them.
Save the section/profile.
Validate mandatory values and age/terms consistency; recompute risk and safety limits and persist the new profile version.
Choose Update plans or Not now when a diet-affecting change is saved.
Ask before replacing today's and the saved weekly plan. On consent open the update workflow; otherwise retain plans and history.
alternatives: A1 Invalid/incomplete input: identify the field and retain the draft until corrected or cancelled.
A2 Cancel editing: discard that unsaved section; the stored profile remains unchanged.
A3 Account settings: change password, confirm logout, configure/check AI-server address, or complete confirmed account deletion.
A4 Health Connect: check availability, grant required read permissions, display connection/sync status, open install/settings when needed, or disconnect without deleting readings.
A5 High risk/clearance concern: display the relevant advisory and treatment restrictions derived from declared data.
exceptions: E1 Profile retrieval failure: display an unavailable/retry state; dependent diet evaluation applies its documented conservative handling.
E2 Save failure: retain entered values and previous stored profile/limits; offer retry.
E3 Diet refresh failure after a successful profile save: keep the new profile, preserve any plan not successfully replaced and explain the partial/failure result.
notes: Required body fields: age, gender, weight and height. Current input bounds: age13–120, weight20–635 kg, height80–272 cm and combined BMI7–200.
Selectable conditions and food exclusions come from current lookup data. OTHER and retired dietary labels remain compatibility records, not new selections.
Risk is derived from declared conditions/status and limitations. Predicted risk does not rewrite this profile.
Connect watch is accessed from Tracking; Health Connect account settings and direct-watch pairing are separate sources.

title: View Health Report
description: Review saved health-score factors, supported condition-risk indications, metric forecasts, anomalies and explanations, with access to Health insights and reminders.
pre: The patient is authenticated. The report may open with no data; each calculation checks its own required inputs.
post: Available results and alerts are displayed; withheld, unavailable and older saved results remain distinguishable. No treatment or declared safety limit is changed.
flow: Open Health Report or refresh it.
Load account-owned profile, readings, meals, exercise history and saved analyses; show progress.
Review score and factor cards.
Calculate/request applicable results; show missing-data reasons when coverage is insufficient.
Open a condition or metric forecast.
Request only supported risk outputs and forecasts with at least14 readings for the metric; preserve model versions and explain missing inputs.
Inspect an alert or trend.
Display measured values, recorded dates, forecast uncertainty and the Conclusion/Analysis/Suggested next step; route high-severity alerts through the existing warning flow.
Open Health insights, reminders or notification history.
Navigate to the selected workflow; preserve the original report's forecast-input scope.
alternatives: A1 Insufficient/unsupported data: withhold that score, risk or forecast and name the missing input rather than inventing a healthy result.
A2 View historical/saved result: identify its date and stale state when a refresh has failed.
A3 High-severity alert: display the warning and existing advice to consult a healthcare professional.
A4 Manage reminders/history: create/edit/disable/delete reminders and inspect persistent notification history through their existing screens.
A5 Advanced summaries: enter UC610, UC620, UC630 or UC640 from Health insights.
exceptions: E1 Retrieval failure: retain available loaded/saved results and mark missing sections; offer retry.
E2 AI-server timeout/error: show the last available result as saved/stale where available; do not create a fresh forecast.
E3 Session change: discard delayed results belonging to the previous account.
notes: Forecast horizon7days; metric minimum14readings. These are application/model prerequisites, not clinical validation.
Analysis requests contain de-identified features and an authentication header, without an account identifier in the payload.
Risk is assessed only for supported condition/model combinations. A direction or score band does not establish a diagnosis or recovery.
Health-insights demo exclusion applies to that hub and its PDF, not automatically to the existing forecast inputs.
Reminder delivery depends on device permission/platform scheduling; persistent alert history remains separately available.

title: Track Health
description: Enter or import supported measurements and inspect biometric/exercise history, source times, counts and interactive graphs.
pre: The patient is authenticated. Manual entry needs no wearable; Health Connect/direct-watch import additionally needs available source permissions/connectivity.
post: Accepted records are stored with original measurement/source metadata; counts/graphs refresh. Duplicate, invalid and unavailable records are not reported as new measurements.
flow: Open Tracking and select Pressure, Glucose, Weight or Exercise.
Load the default30-day account history, summary, source state and completed-session history; restore the saved watch selection where available.
Choose an existing graph point, period or zoom control.
Render the selected range; show a vertical line and point details only for an actual matched record.
Choose Add reading and enter values, context and time.
Validate required values, configured plausibility and future-date tolerance; preserve the form on failure.
Save the reading.
Persist the manual source, refresh history/summary and expose the updated data to analysis.
Connect/import a health source or leave the signed-in app active.
Read only supported available saved records, validate/deduplicate, store original recorded_at plus first imported_at, and display new-record counts and successful-check state.
alternatives: A1 Health Connect: request supported read permissions and import returned records. Initial lookback is90days; later reads overlap the last successful check by5minutes to catch delayed inserts. The overlap does not subtract5minutes from measurement time.

A2 Direct watch: disconnect competing companion-app ownership first, keep Bluetooth on, scan/select a supported device and read available saved history. Do not assume every visible watch value is stored/exposed.
A3 Active-app sync: check Health Connect about once/minute and direct-watch saved history about every15seconds; resume triggers a check. Skip overlapping checks and retry after temporary failures.
A4 Exercise: choose By session or Daily total; inspect sessions, exact completion times and available metadata. Unknown durations are labelled and excluded from minute plots/totals.
A5 Change period: use7/30/90days or a valid custom range, then zoom/pan/reset; touching a gap clears selected details.
A6 Delete a reading: confirm removal; refresh on success and restore the visible row on write failure.
A7 Disconnect a source: stop future checks without deleting stored measurements.
exceptions: E1 Source/permission unavailable: show install/settings or disconnect-first guidance; keep existing history and manual entry available.
E2 No new saved watch record: report a successful zero-new-record check rather than promise immediate delivery.
E3 Save/import failure: retain previous records and form/draft state; do not report rejected/duplicate rows as imported.
E4 Exercise retrieval failure: show Unavailable and Retry rather than zero completed sessions.
notes: Metrics: blood pressure, glucose and weight only when the selected adapter actually exposes measured records.
Duplicate key: account + metric + original UTC timestamp. Nearby equal-valued readings remain separate.
Record time and first import time are distinct; last successful source check can advance with zero new rows.
No continuous OS background sync or guaranteed watch latency is implemented.
Exercise history is read from owned completed treatment sessions; manual biometric entry does not fabricate exercise completions.

title: View Food Information and Log Meal
description: Build a meal from a camera/gallery image or manual catalogue search, review every food/quantity, inspect advice and explicitly save what was eaten.
pre: The patient is authenticated. Camera/gallery permission is needed only for that image source; manual logging remains available.
post: On successful Save, the meal, nutrient snapshots, reviewed recognition metadata and optional photo are stored. Daily totals and plan comparison refresh; a cancelled/failed draft is not silently saved.
flow: Select Log meal and choose camera, gallery or manual entry.
Retrieve current diet context and show the brief saved-plan reminder.
Capture/select a photo, or search a catalogue food.
Validate a photo as JPEG/PNG≤10MB with original sides≥224px; prepare orientation-corrected JPEG quality80 at most1024px on the long edge. Manual entry skips photo permission and recognition.
Wait for recognition or choose foods manually.

Call the authenticated owned server with image/codes. Map returned foods to catalogue entries; show multiple items, estimated counts/total grams, warnings and review state. Auto/local fallback follows server configuration.
Correct foods, add missed sides, change count/total grams or remove an item.

Merge identical foods within this meal; reject invalid combined meal-entry portions, recalculate catalogue nutrients and reassess current-profile verdicts. Keep count × unit estimate consistent with total grams.
Optionally explore What if I change this meal? and return a proposal.
Run UC810 without altering saved history or silently saving the draft.
Review the actual meal and press Save.
Store the photo only with the confirmed meal, retain historical core nutrient snapshots and recognition metadata, update totals and refresh plan-related feedback.
alternatives: A1 Low confidence/non-food/empty result: explain the limitation and continue through manual catalogue search.
A2 Online vision unavailable: when configured auto mode can use local recognition, state that local portions are standard servings and require review; otherwise offer retry/manual entry.
A3 Count/weight review: edit total edible grams in10–1000g and optional supported count; e.g. two250g cups imply500g total before user correction.
A4 Duplicate add: merge the same food's grams and re-evaluate warnings rather than append a duplicate line.
A5 History: filter dates, open full meal details, tap a photo for an entire-image viewer, or confirm meal/photo deletion.
A6 Cancel: discard the unsaved image/draft; successful saved history remains unchanged.
A7 Health conflict: display the reason/red warning while allowing the patient to log actual intake.
exceptions: E1 Invalid/unreadable image or permission refusal: explain the problem and allow another source/manual entry.
E2 Recognition timeout/provider failure: stop the waiting state and offer retry/manual logging; do not fabricate detections or amounts.
E3 Meal/photo persistence failure: undo the optimistic visible save, retain the review draft and allow retry.
E4 Session/draft changes during asynchronous work: ignore outdated results instead of attaching them to another account or meal.
notes: Nutrition comes from catalogue food rows × confirmed grams; image weights/counts remain estimates.
Local model confidence uses the0.60 review threshold. Online confidence is an uncalibrated estimate and never a measured portion.
An owned-server request carries image and declared codes; the optional external vision provider receives only prepared image/catalogue context, not profile codes or account/session identifiers.
The recognition client uses a30-second configured timeout per network phase; a5-second online result is not guaranteed.
Model version is retained as provenance; no model name needs to be shown in the patient UI.
Confirming Save marks review metadata as reviewed; it does not verify the image estimate as a measured quantity.

title: View Food Recommendation and Manage Diet Plan
description: Review food suitability and plan rationale; load, generate or edit today's/weekly/future plans while keeping AI validation separate from patient-choice warnings.
pre: The patient is authenticated. Current profile/limits are retrieved; unavailable data invokes conservative handling and limits confidence in personalised advice.
post: Only a fully validated AI result is newly saved. Structurally valid patient choices can be saved with warnings. Existing plans/logged history survive cancelled or failed generation.
flow: Open Today's plan or Weekly plan.
Load the applicable saved plan; weekly view initially focuses today's local date. Display date, food details, target coverage and red warnings.
Select Generate, Replan or Plan the rest of today.
Retrieve current profile, locked rows, logged meals and food history; show progress and send a de-identified planning request.
Wait for the proposed plan.
Check every AI-chosen portion, all requested dates, lower nutrition needs and upper/profile gates. Count today's actual logged intake once; reject and retry up to3attempts if invalid.
Review the resulting foods and reasons.
Save only after all generation gates pass; display shortfalls/conflicts and retain an explanatory no-new-plan outcome when no candidate passes.
Add, replace, resize, remove or lock a chosen food.
Show that food/date's own details. Patient-selected choices are advisory: merge repeated food portions and highlight health conflicts in red; malformed portions/dates remain blocking.
Choose a previous date or a future start/end period.
Open saved history without automatic generation, or generate1–31future inclusive days in validated blocks and save the assembled period only when every block succeeds.
alternatives: A1 Build my own plan: use the same food-card/slot layout and catalogue search independently of AI availability; show nutrition/profile warnings and reject only structural errors/empty choices.
A2 Future plan: choose1day,1week,1month preset or explicit dates; require start after today and at most31inclusive days.
A3 Earlier plan: daily plan takes precedence over overlapping weekly/multi-day plans; keep the chosen date visible.
A4 Profile update prompt: regenerate current/saved weekly plans only after the patient's consent from UC300; keep logs and any plan not successfully replaced.
A5 Locked food conflict: locks survive normal regeneration but do not bypass current-profile AI validation; explain why a locked configuration cannot be generated.
A6 Compare adherence: open UC910 for recorded food/portion differences and daily/weekly next-meal options.
A7 Alternative suggestion: offer suitable catalogue choices, while still allowing the patient to select another food with advisory warnings.
exceptions: E1 AI unavailable/timeout or3invalid attempts: keep the saved plan and offer retry/manual building.
E2 Future generation block failure: do not persist a partial requested period or replace saved plans with it.
E3 Invalid structural edit or failed write: retain the draft/previous plan and explain the specific failure.
E4 Profile unavailable: state conservative limits and uncertainty; never claim full personalised suitability.
notes: AI generation must satisfy75% minimum energy coverage plus applicable nutrient needs and current upper limits; patient choices can remain saved with a visible shortfall warning.
All planned dates use device-local calendar days. Future scheduling is1–31inclusive days, not an unbounded annual planner.
A20-second timeout applies per plan API request; retries and future blocks add elapsed time.
Weekly/default plans are seven days; multi-day scheduled plans reuse the existing daily/weekly storage type with explicit start/end dates.
Limited catalogue/exclusion combinations can prevent an adequate varied plan. Failure is explicit rather than a guaranteed promise of a completely different menu.
Manual choices, even Build my own plan, are advisory in the current application; older strict-manual descriptions are superseded.

title: Retrieve Profile Information
description: Return the authenticated account's profile, declared conditions/status, food exclusions, limitations and derived limits with an explicit availability/completeness status.
pre: An including workflow needs account-scoped profile context. Without a current authenticated account the request fails.
post: The including workflow receives the correct account's snapshot/status or a conservative unavailable result; missing values are not invented.
flow: The use case begins when an including workflow requests profile context. Resolve the authenticated account internally; do not accept another patient's arbitrary identifier.
Read the profile and required saved limits; identify absent/incomplete/error states.
Return complete or stale profile/limits, or available fields with conservative limits for missing/incomplete data.
The caller uses status appropriately: explain conservative handling and withhold personalised food increases where a usable profile is unavailable.
alternatives: A1 No profile: return NOT_CONFIGURED and conservative limits; the UI directs the patient to setup.
A2 Incomplete profile: return existing fields and conservative limits with INCOMPLETE; do not fill demographics with guessed values.
A3 Stale profile: return the stored profile with STALE after182days and allow the caller to request review.
exceptions: E1 No active session: return authentication failure and no other account's data.
E2 Repository failure: return ERROR/conservative limits. This service does not promise a cached profile or a profile-access audit-log write.
E3 Account changes during a calling workflow: the ViewModel discards the delayed result and requests sign-in/reload.
notes: Returned data includes account-scoped profile/version/update time, supported declarations and safety limits; account identifiers stay in the application/backend ownership boundary.
RiskAssessmentService is the shared implementation. It does not create a separate profile-access-log record.
Complete and stale snapshots use stored limits or regenerate them from the saved profile when needed; missing/incomplete/error snapshots use conservative limits.
Included by profile, meal, planning, diet-review and health-analysis workflows as their required context.

title: Review Health Timeline
description: Inspect plans, logged meals, readings, exercises and symptom diary entries on a shared local-day timeline.
pre: An authenticated account is available; the screen can open with empty or partially unavailable history.
post: Selected records/nearby observations are displayed without changing saved records.
flow: Open Health insights > Timeline and select a week/day.
Load account-owned records and build dated events with demo/availability labels.
Filter lanes, zoom or select a marker.
Draw a selected-time line, display original event details and show available nearby readings as temporal observations.
Change the presentation-data switch or day.
Rebuild the visible events for the chosen scope without deleting stored rows.
alternatives: A1 A plan's suggested meal time or a diary noon marker is a display position, not a measurement timestamp.
A2 Empty day: display a clear no-records state, not zero intake or zero symptoms.
exceptions: E1 Missing source: show notices and available events; offer refresh.
E2 Session change: discard delayed data from the prior account.
notes: Original measurement/completion times are retained.
The demo filter affects Health insights and its PDF only.
Temporal proximity does not prove a dietary or treatment effect.

title: Review and Export Weekly Progress
description: Review the selected week's conclusions, evidence and food guidance and export an offline PDF.
pre: An authenticated account is available; enough logged evidence is needed only for the individual comparisons that require it.
post: A PDF is prepared from the same loaded facts when export succeeds; cancelling the native dialog changes no records.
flow: Open Weekly report and select an elapsed week.
Build applicable-plan comparisons, coverage, diet/activity facts and context-separated reading changes.
Expand food advice or supporting dates.
Show daily portions, weekly occurrence totals and current-profile assumptions; supporting dates open matching timeline evidence.
Choose Export / print PDF.
Generate local PDF bytes from the same snapshot and invoke the device print/export UI.
alternatives: A1 No comparable meals: state what is missing and omit a fabricated adherence percentage.
A2 Incomplete days/different coverage: qualify averages and comparisons; missing logs remain unknown.
A3 Cancel the system dialog: retain the weekly screen and stored records.
exceptions: E1 PDF/native dialog unavailable: show a retry message; do not claim an export was completed.
E2 Partial history retrieval: include the same notices in screen and PDF.
notes: Previous-period summaries use equal elapsed calendar windows and daily means for reading changes; glucose contexts stay separate.
Presentation records remain labelled and can be excluded locally.
No online narrative service is required for these deterministic explanations.

title: Review Data Quality
description: Inspect available readings, import provenance, coverage gaps and input minimums.
pre: The patient is authenticated; no readings are required to open the dashboard.
post: Source/check/coverage information is shown; no measurement or forecast is fabricated.
flow: Open Health insights > Data quality.
Load selected-week and supporting history with saved source/sync metadata.
Inspect a metric, import group or missing date.
Display counts, original/import times, latest per-metric data and missing coverage.
Toggle presentation inclusion or refresh.
Recalculate this hub/PDF scope without modifying stored data or existing Health Report inputs.
alternatives: A1 No readings for a metric: state unavailable/missing rather than normal health.
A2 A successful source check with0newrecords remains distinct from failure.
exceptions: E1 Source state/history retrieval fails: show a notice and mark completeness uncertain.
notes: Input minimums describe availability, not guaranteed predictive accuracy.
Watch records depend on actual supported source capability.

title: Manage Recovery Check In
description: Record daily patient-reported pain, stiffness and exercise difficulty alongside an owned treatment assignment.
pre: The patient is authenticated and has an owned treatment assignment for the selected diary date.
post: One account/assignment/date entry is saved or an explicitly confirmed entry is deleted; treatment progress remains unchanged.
flow: Open Recovery and choose Add recovery check-in or an existing date.
Load owned assignments and existing diary values.
Choose date and enter pain/stiffness/difficulty/optional notes.
Validate date from assignment start through today, score ranges and500-character note limit.
Save the check-in.
Insert or update the same logical account/assignment/date row using the repository and backend ownership checks.
Review symptoms and completed exercise evidence.
Compare diary values within that assignment, highlight recent worsening and group posture results by the same exercise.
alternatives: A1 Existing date: edit the same entry rather than create a duplicate.
A2 Delete: require confirmation before repository deletion.
A3 No diary or too few dates: state insufficient evidence; do not infer symptom improvement.
exceptions: E1 Invalid score/date/notes: identify the issue and preserve input.
E2 Retrieval/write/ownership failure: retain prior state, show the failure and offer retry.
notes: Pain/stiffness0–10; difficulty1–5; notes≤500characters.
Database uniqueness: account_id + patient_plan_id + check_in_date; backend dates use Asia/Kuala_Lumpur.
Symptoms are self-reports; neither symptom trends nor posture results automatically advance treatment.

title: Simulate Meal Changes
description: Preview catalogue food/portion changes in an isolated proposal before applying it to the unsaved meal draft.
pre: The patient has an unsaved meal draft in review and current diet context is available or explicitly conservative.
post: The original stays unchanged until Use in meal draft; applying returns a reviewed proposal, not a saved meal.
flow: Choose What if I change this meal? from meal review.
Copy the original items into a separate proposal and display original/proposed nutrient values.
Add/replace/remove foods or edit grams.
Merge duplicate foods, validate meal-entry quantities, recalculate6nutrients and recorded-day totals once, and display suitability/allowance warnings.
Choose Reset, Cancel or Use in meal draft.
Reset/cancel preserve the original; explicit Use returns items only to the matching still-open draft.
Acknowledge a warning proposal when prompted.
Retain the normal review/save action and reassess verdicts in the original workflow.
alternatives: A1 Search suggests currently suitable catalogue foods at standard portions; a changed portion is assessed again.
A2 Reset restores the proposal to its original copy.
exceptions: E1 Invalid/nonfinite quantity: reject the change and keep the previous proposal.
E2 Original draft/session changed: refuse stale application rather than overwrite another meal.
notes: The simulator calculates nutrition; it does not predict glucose/BP response.
Warnings do not silently save or edit meal history.

title: Compare Planned and Logged Meals
description: Explain meal differences and derive specific daily and weekly food options from current profile rules and recorded evidence.
pre: The patient is authenticated. A fair adherence comparison needs an applicable plan saved before the relevant logged meal; the screen can still show missing/reference states.
post: The selected week/day shows food grams, nutrient differences, coverage and supported options; no historical log or plan is automatically changed.
flow: Open Diet review > Plan comparison and choose a week/day.
Load account meals and saved plans, select the applicable daily/overlapping multi-day plan and match local date/meal slot/food key.
Inspect a day, meal or nutrient.
Show close/portion/food-change, missing/not-due, unplanned, reference-only or unavailable status; expose planned/logged quantities and deltas.
Read daily food review and weekly priorities.
Name foods and review portions with nutrient reasons, affected dates/counts and current-profile suitability checks.
Open a supporting record or meal simulation.
Show the source record/isolated proposal; retain explicit review and Save control.
alternatives: A1 Plan generated after the logged meal: display reference-only; exclude it from adherence evidence.
A2 Missing/partial meals: mark unknown coverage and avoid diagnosing deficiency from sparse logs.
A3 Repeated choices: sum occurrences/grams actually observed, without extrapolating an extra weekly allowance.
A4 Exploratory meal/reading patterns: show only when12pairs across7days and variation criteria pass; label the association non-causal.
exceptions: E1 Plans unavailable or invalid amounts: show Cannot compare and retry instead of a false denominator.
E2 Missing/incomplete profile: withhold personalised increases; retain recorded comparisons.
E3 Unsafe increase or unsupported kidney-sensitive advice: withhold the option; a required replacement must be explicit and self-contained.
notes: Daily plans precede weekly plans, then latest start/generated time resolves overlap.
Changed portions differ by more than10% of planned grams, with the configured small rounding tolerance.
Core logged nutrients remain snapshots; catalogue extras are labelled estimates.
Up to4daily options and6weekly groups keep the guidance bounded. Options are not a deficiency diagnosis or an automatic prescription.
